Use case: precise-object-edit / conservative painted surface simplification.
Edit target: the attached transparent 3 by 3 atlas of nine ornate biological weapon organs from a game.
Make a carefully restrained production paintover, about 20% simpler in SURFACE HIGHLIGHTS AND MICROTEXTURE ONLY. Preserve the original sophisticated sculpted insect forms.

Change: consolidate clusters of tiny glossy white pinpricks into fewer, wider, soft-edged painted reflection shapes. Remove roughly one fifth of the smallest scratchy mottling, granular flecks and secondary micro-veins, filling those areas with their surrounding local colour. Simplify the internal shape of reflections rather than just making everything darker. Preserve large and medium-scale chitin plates, bone ridges, red mandible teeth, sac lobes, channels, wings, major veins and broad light/shadow modelling. The image should visibly have cleaner, quieter surfaces at full size while retaining 75–90% of the original richness.

Invariants: EXACTLY the same nine objects, silhouettes, number and shape of spikes/teeth/lobes, proportions, pose, orientation, scale, layout and relative pixel placement. Keep every tip, claw and transparent gap. Do not rearrange or crop anything. Preserve the original bright colours, hues, saturation, overall luminance and energy: orange, red, green, cyan/blue, violet and pink remain vivid. Bone stays ivory and chitin stays deep navy. Do not dim the atlas, desaturate it or add a sepia filter. Keep volume, craftsmanship and crisp detailed silhouettes.
Do not make icons, vectors, thick black cartoons, flat single-colour shapes, posterization, a children's drawing, plastic toy forms or minimalist symbols. Do not erase all texture or all shading.
Output: the full original square atlas, preferably exactly 1254 by 1254 pixels, genuinely transparent background. No background, text, labels, borders, new objects, glow around silhouettes or watermark. Alter the original image in place rather than redesigning it.
